entries.claim: In Fisher's tea experiment 8 cups contain 4 milk-first, giving C(8,4)=70 equally likely guesses and 1/70 for all-correct
entries.notes: Combinatorics is exact; the all-correct outcome is Fisher's own later account

entries.claim: Null distribution of guessed cups is 1/70, 16/70, 36/70, 16/70, 1/70 for 0-4 correct
Null and alternative hypotheses are the two competing statements a test chooses between
entries.notes: Direction must be fixed before seeing data

entries.claim: The p-value is the probability, assuming H0 is true, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed one
entries.notes: Conditional on H0; not P(H0 | data)

entries.claim: The 0.05 significance convention traces to Fisher's 1925 recommendation of a 1-in-20 standard
entries.locator: ASA statement on p-values, historical context
entries.notes: Convention, not a law; level should depend on context

entries.claim: Type I error (rejecting a true H0) has probability alpha; type II error (not rejecting a false H0) has probability beta; power is 1-beta
entries.locator: NIST/SEMATECH, Type I and II errors
entries.notes: Power increases with sample size; alpha and beta trade off

entries.claim: The ASA statement cautions against using p < 0.05 as an automatic decision rule and stresses effect size and context
entries.notes: Optional stopping inflates the Type I error rate

entries.claim: Two-sided normal p-value for a z statistic shown interactively
entries.notes: Normal approximation via an erf series; small samples should use t
